reports.title: Cold Front Alters Fishing Scene - Mild Days Soon to Return
reports.text:
Winter winds are coming, says the weatherman, that may put the brakes on the wonderful fall fishing that had crappie anglers scoring good stringers plus nice catches reported by catfishermen lately along the main river channel.
Decent numbers of crappie had been showing up in the creel as they dunked jigs tipped with minnows in midrange depths of 9 to 14 feet.
Bass fishing has been fair for anglers tossing Rattle Traps, shallow running crankbaits, twister tail grubs and some aggressive topwater at times. Gravel banks and big chunk rocky points have been producing as have rip-rap levees and gravel roadbeds. It’s time to batten down the hatches and dig out the coveralls and big thick coats if…

reports.title: Scott McGlinchey's Fishing Report
reports.text:
As water temperatures continue to cool, the bass fishing on Kentucky Lake has really improved. We're now catching more quality bass, and it's becoming increasingly common to catch bigger fish than smaller ones.
The topwater bass bite started in late July and has continued right through the summer and into the fall. During August and early September, we caught good numbers of bass, with several different locations producing schooling fish on and off throughout the day.
